events.dn: Applications are taken January through October, so apply this month
events.ct: TheMarket@MTxFCM.com (put your business name in the subject)
events.nt: Cottage food is the point of this market and the page lists nuts as an example. Oct 31 is their Fall Harvest Festival with extra vendors and traffic. A December Christmas Market is on their site with no date yet.
events.x: 10x20 is $45, 10x30 is $55. Attend weekly, every other week, monthly or special events only. Insurance not stated.

events.nt: Only food covered by the Texas Cottage Food law may be sold. The city's food-vendor steps mention a health permit application; ask whether a registered cottage vendor needs it. Closed Thanksgiving weekend. Season runs to Dec 12.
events.x: Tent legs weighted 25 lb per corner. A product sample may be requested. Older 2023 rules said no fee, so confirm the $10.

events.nt: Closest market to home. The season is listed through Oct 31, so there are four Saturdays left.
events.x: Sponsored by the Midlothian Downtown Business Association. No fee, application or cottage rule found online.

events.nt: One listing says 'no food booths'. That may mean prepared food only, so ask whether packaged cottage food is allowed. Oct 24 overlaps Autumn Daze downtown.
events.x: Apply through the city's OpenGov portal. Guidelines are PDFs linked from the city page.

events.v: Front Street Station, 100 W Front St
events.nt: Cottage foods are explicitly allowed (canned goods, spices, candy, baked goods). The pages never state a year or last date; the 2025 season ended Nov 29. Being a market vendor is also the likely way into Christmas on the Square (Dec 1).
events.x: Apply once for the season, request dates, then pay within 72 hours of each invoice to hold the date. Tables covered, items labeled with name and price.

events.v: City lot at Front & Center, 300 W Front St

events.x: Run by Four Seasons Markets for the city. The city lists baked goods and jams among artisan goods.

events.fee: $35 application; stall fees are in a handbook that isn't public

events.x: Food handler card and general liability insurance are required after approval. Booth fees aren't public.

events.fee: Artisan Alley $200 for every Saturday ($100 alternating); indoor $300 ($150 alternating)

events.x: Setup 7:30-8:50am, vehicles out by 8:35am, down by 2pm. Bring tables, canopy, chairs and weights. Season pass is $180, not worth it with one date left.

events.n: Markets for Makers: Austin Holiday (Fair Market)
events.fee: $50 non-refundable application fee, then a booth fee on acceptance (not published) plus 3.99% processing
events.adm: About $8, tiered by arrival time (VIP $20, kids under 12 free). 2026 Austin price not re-confirmed.
events.comp: Category caps. Specialty foods is its own category.
events.nt: 'Specialty foods' is an official category and each category has a vendor cap, which protects you from copycats. Food terms live in the vendor T&Cs, which I could not read. Needs a hotel night or two.
events.x: Juried in rolling waves. Decisions come about a month before the show, so a mid-November answer for this one. Same organizer runs Houston Nov 14-15 (about 250 mi).

events.fee: $50 application fee plus booth fee on acceptance (not published)

events.comp: Category caps. Specialty foods is its own category.
events.dn: Watch the organizer site for the next Dallas date
events.nt: Closest ticketed makers market to home. The Feb 2026 lineup included a cookie vendor, so food makers get in. Apply as soon as a Dallas date appears.

events.n: Braum's An Affair of the Heart: Oklahoma City (Feb 2027)
events.fee: $6 per sq ft: 10x10 is $659 including the $59 listing fee. Corner +$75.
events.adm: $14 weekend pass (visitokc says $13), kids 12 and under free, parking free
events.attn: OKC not published. Tulsa edition projects 26,000.
events.comp: Food and Beverage is 1 of 14 categories. Counts not published.
events.dn: No published deadline. Call 405-632-2652 now to get on the list
events.nt: This is the 'Heart of Affair' Brandy meant. Biggest crowd of any show here but a 3.5-hour drive, a hotel and a $659 booth, so you need roughly 45 jars just to cover booth and trip. Attendance for OKC is not published; the number used is the Tulsa edition's projection.
events.x: Juried, handmade preferred. A waiting list is typical. $1M certificate of insurance and an Oklahoma sales tax permit are required. Ask whether a Texas cottage food producer can sell in Oklahoma. Food-vendor paperwork for the Oct 23-25 show was due Sep 18, so that one is closed.

events.n: Braum's An Affair of the Heart: Tulsa
events.fee: Same organizer pricing as OKC, about $659 for a 10x10 (Tulsa rate not verified)
events.comp: 'Gourmet foods' is a listed vendor type
events.nt: Beyond the 250-mile range. Listed for completeness.
events.x: Waitlist-only is typical.

events.n: Home for the Holidays Gift Market: Waco
events.fee: Only in the vendor portal. 33% deposit, 33% at 90 days, 33% at 60 days out.
events.adm: $6 to $10 weekend wristband, kids 12 and under free
events.comp: Organizer limits categories and spreads same-category vendors apart.
events.dn: No deadline. Returning vendors have first right; ask for the cancellation list
events.nt: Likely full. Their stated policy is to limit product categories and spread out vendors of the same category, which is what you want. Specialty foods is a listed category.
events.x: Same series as the Waxahachie Hollydays Market (Oct 9-11) and Plano (Oct 16-18). Katy Nov 20-22, Humble Dec 4-5 and Rosenberg Dec 4-6 are later stops.

events.adm: $10 to $15 via Humanitix, weekend re-entry, kids under 12 free

events.x: Franchise show with 'upscale vintage, handmade and consumables'. The East Texas edition is in Tyler Nov 6-8 (about 110 mi).
